messages:
maria: FYI I flipped the flag fuse_latebind_prefetch=true on the dev cluster to test epilogue late-binding for QKV-packed fused-attn. Seeing a weird perf regression for short-context interactive workloads (seq_len<=16) on A100-80GB.
jon: Curious — regression in latency or throughput? numbers?
maria: P95 latency up ~18% on small batches (batch sizes 1-8). Throughput drops ~10% for mixed-load queues. Long sequences (>128) look fine.
devan: Any stack traces or profiler output? Could be register pressure or L2 thrash from the prefetch reordering.
maria: Attached quick flame from nvprof run: https://internal.perf/2468/flame-latebind.svg (opaque link, has a big red hump in epilogue kernel). Also paste of smstats: 
```
Kernel: fused_attn_epilogue
Avg regs per thread: 64 -> 88 (when flag on)
SM occupancy: 0.45 -> 0.32
L2 read bandwidth spike concurrent with epilogue
```
jon: 64->88 regs is huge. Late-binding probably inlined extra paths for rope/bias conditional handlers. That will reduce occupancy on A100 and hurt latency for small batches.
lee: Did we accidentally enable both prefetch and latebind epilogue fusion together? I remember a toggle that collapses bias/rope and also does page-aware prefetch.
maria: Yes both toggles are on in the experiment: fuse_latebind_prefetch + epilogue_fuse_bias_rope = true. I wanted to test combined win.
devan: For mixed batch workloads the per-request latency sensitive paths get worse because occupancy drop increases per-token serialization. For longer seqs amortization helps so we saw no harm.
infra-bot: deploy-check: dev pool a100-80gb-02 passed smoke, but perf regression flagged by canary monitors at 12:03 UTC (alert id perf-246800).
jon: Ok immediate rollback for canary, but we should collect microbench artifacts. Maria can you re-run microbench with these variants and include kernel cycles and register usage? Use the harness: 
```
./perf/harness --kernel fused_attn_epilogue --seqs 4,8,16,64,128 --bs 1,4,8,32 --flags latebind,prefetch,epilogue_biasrope
```
maria: Running now, will dump csv to /tmp/latebind-microbench.csv and upload. Quick note: the fused path also touches paged-KV code path which has an independent prefetch so might be doubling prefetches.
devan: Bingo. Doubling prefetch + latebind conditionals likely triggered register spill or spilled locals into local memory causing L1/L2 pressure. Check for increased local mem transactions in nvprof.
lee: Another angle — our kernel chooser sometimes picks sgemm-fused variant vs vectorized epilogue based on heuristics. The latebind change might have nudged the heuristic boundary; need to ensure chooser sees register footprint estimates.
maria: Microbench results (high-level): seq=4, bs=1: cycles 1.18x baseline; seq=128, bs=32: cycles 0.99x baseline. NVTX shows extra branches in epilogue. I also captured PTX disasm for the epilogue segment; will attach.
jon: Proposed next steps: 
- revert canary immediately (done)
- add a static estimate of regs-per-thread in kernel metadata so chooser can avoid low-occupancy variants for small batches
- split latebind into two passes: (1) prefetch scheduling only, (2) epilogue merging, test independently
- add microbench gating for regressions under seq<=16 bs<=8
Can we get owners for each?
devan: I can own the static-regs metadata and update chooser heuristics. I'll add a quick model: expected_regs = base + (rope? 8:0) + (bias? 4:0) + (latebind? 16:0) — tune after.
maria: I'll iterate on split flags and re-run microbench. Will also add NVPROF counters for local mem loads/stores.
lee: I'll add a unit in kernel chooser test that enumerates combos and asserts occupancy >= 0.4 for tiny batches unless the expected win > 1.1x.
jon: Also record a note in the changelog about register pressure tradeoffs for fused epilogue paths (so infra/sre aware).
infra-bot: ticket created perf-246800: "Investigate latebind prefetch+epilogue fusion regression on A100 small-batch latencies" assigned to maria, devan, lee.
maria: Thanks. Uploading artifacts now: /artifacts/2468/latebind-microbench.csv, /artifacts/2468/epilogue-ptx.s, /artifacts/2468/nvprof.log
jon: Great. Once we have tuned expected_regs and split flags, let's re-run canary with a controlled sample and ramp if no regressions.
maria: Plan: split flags today, new metrics by EOD, microbench+canary tomorrow.
devan: FYI I'll add a quick synthetic that simulates mixed interactive load to our perf-regression runner so this doesn't slip through.
lee: sounds good — thanks team :thumbsup:
